messages.subject: AKDE and KDE
parts:
Hi Chris, I'm trying to use ctmm to calculate home ranges. I had already calculated KDE using code from a movement workshop- and I'm getting values that are really different from the KDE values ctmm gives me. Can't really understand if it's a matter of the grid, or what's causing it.  This is the grid and KDE function I was using originally for reference:

ext <- extent(guana)
multiplyers <- c((ext[2]-ext[1])*0.2, (ext[4]-ext[3])*0.2)   #adding 20% around the edges
ext <- extend(ext, multiplyers)
grd <- raster(ext)
res(grd) <- 250   #resolution
projection(grd) <- proj4string(guana) #this projection is in UTM- so it's different from
                                                                     the one my data has in ctmm   
kern <- kernelUD(guana[,"id"], h="href",
                 grid=as(grd, "SpatialPixels"), kern="bivnorm")
kernHR <- kernel.area(kern, percent = c(50, 95, 99), unin="m", unout="km2")

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: AKDE and KDE
parts:
Hi Malena,

I'm not exactly clear on the question. You want to know why your ctmm KDE (not AKDE?) estimates are different from the adehabitat KDE estimates (using the above code)? There are many possible differences here:
  1. adehabitat's "href" bandwidth optimizer is the rule-of-thumb method, while ctmm's IID bandwidth optimizer is the GRF method. Neither of these is really better than the other and they should be pretty close for large n.
  2. adehabitat's kernel and reference covariance is circular, while ctmm's kernel and reference covariance may be circular or elliptical, depending on which model is selected (isotropic or anisotropic). Elliptical can be preferable for animals with elongated home ranges, but often times it's not a big difference.
  3. By default, ctmm applies a GRF bias correction to both the AKDE and KDE areas ( https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12673 ). This can yield a big improvement for small n.
  4. If the data are autocorrelated, AKDE can be much larger (with much more uncertainty) than KDE from either package.
  5. If the data have substantial location error (and you model that), then the ctmm AKDEs and KDEs will shrink appropriately.
Does this answer your question?

Best,
Chris
